mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes GLC43 AMG engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt M276 V6 engine for the GLC43 costs £4,500-£8,000 supply-only; a rebuilt M139l four-cylinder costs £6,000-£9,000 supply-only. Fitting adds £1,000-£2,000 depending on complexity - AMG engines require specialist knowledge.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of camshaft adjuster failure on a Mercedes GLC43?

acceptedAnswer.text: A 1-3 second metallic rattling noise on cold start is the classic warning sign on the M276 V6. If ignored, it can lead to rough idle, misfires, check engine lights, and eventually catastrophic engine failure.

mainEntity.name: Is the Mercedes GLC43 V6 engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - the M276 is widely regarded as one of the most reliable Mercedes engines of the last 20 years. The camshaft adjuster issue is the only significant weak point, and it's well understood by specialists. With proper maintenance, the M276 routinely exceeds 150,000 miles.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Mercedes GLC43 engine last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Properly maintained M276 V6 engines routinely reach 150,000-200,000 miles before major work. The M139l four-cylinder is too new for definitive long-term data, but early indications suggest similar longevity with proper maintenance.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in my Mercedes GLC43?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the GLC43 is otherwise in good condition with no rust or major electrical faults. A rebuilt M276 costs £4,500-£8,000 - far less than replacing a £25,000-£40,000 vehicle. The GLC43's strong residual values make engine replacement financially justifiable.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the V6 GLC43 and the new four-cylinder GLC43?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 2016-2022 GLC43 uses the M276 3.0L twin-turbo V6 (367-390hp) with a characterful AMG soundtrack. The 2024-present GLC43 uses the M139l 2.0L turbo four-cylinder with electric turbocharger and 48V mild hybrid (416hp) - more power, fewer cylinders, and a very different character.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes Benz GLC Class GLC43 - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The GLC43 AMG joined the GLC range in 2016 as the performance entry point below the V8-powered GLC63. Powered by the M276 3.0-litre twin-turbo V6, it delivered 367hp and a characterful AMG soundtrack. In 2024, the second-generation X254 GLC43 replaced the V6 with the M139l 2.0-litre four-cylinder featuring an electrically assisted turbocharger and 48V mild-hybrid system - more power, fewer cylinders, and a dramatically different character.

milestones.description: M276.823, 3.0L twin-turbo V6, 390hp (facelift X253/C253, increased output)
X253 GLC43 production ends; V6 discontinued
M139l, 2.0L turbo four-cylinder with electric turbocharger and 48V mild hybrid, 416hp (X254 GLC43)

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes Benz GLC Class GLC43 Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The GLC43's M276 twin-turbo V6 is widely regarded as one of Mercedes' most reliable modern engines, but it has one well-documented Achilles' heel - camshaft adjuster wear that manifests as a cold-start rattle. The newer M139l four-cylinder is too recent for definitive failure data, but its complexity (electric turbocharger, 48V system) introduces new potential failure points. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: M276 Camshaft Adjuster (Phaser) Failure - The Cold-Start Rattle
problems.rootCause: The intake camshaft adjusters (phasers) can break internally, causing the timing to drift. A metallic rattling noise on cold start is the classic symptom. If ignored, incorrect cam phasing can cause poor combustion, rough idle, misfires, and accelerated timing chain wear.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace both intake camshaft adjusters, reseal timing covers, new oil and filter. 12-14 hour job.
repairOptions.longevity: If caught early with no other damage

repairOptions.tier: Full Replacement - Rebuilt M276 engine with revised adjusters
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt M276 engine with factory-revised adjusters, precision balancing, new timing chain and guides, AMG-specific calibration
repairOptions.longevity: If adjuster failure has caused camshaft or valve damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2016-2022 GLC43 AMG 4MATIC is worth approximately £25,000-£40,000 depending on mileage and condition. The GLC43 sits firmly in the £15,000+ band - replacement cost is typically small relative to vehicle value, making a full rebuilt engine a justifiable investment for owners planning to keep the car.
problems.recommendation: The M276 is a £25,000-£40,000 car at current market values. If the rattle has just started with no metal in the oil or fault codes, the intermediate adjuster replacement is the value play - find a specialist who has done this job before. If the engine has been run with adjuster failure to the point of camshaft pulse wheel damage or codes persist after adjuster replacement, step up to a full rebuilt unit from an AMG specialist. Never use non-OEM adjusters on this engine - they fail within 10,000 miles.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M276 Mercedes GLC43 engine prices

problems.h4: M276 Oil Leaks - Timing Covers and Camshaft Sensors
problems.rootCause: The M276 can develop oil leaks from the front upper timing covers and camshaft position sensors. These leaks are not catastrophic but can lead to oil contamination of electrical components and, if ignored, low oil pressure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace camshaft position sensors and seals, clean wiring harness
Reseal upper timing covers, replace gaskets and seals
repairOptions.longevity: If oil is pooling on the engine or dripping

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt M276 engine with new seals throughout
repairOptions.longevity: If oil loss has caused bottom-end damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: As above - a typical GLC43 is worth £25,000-£40,000.
problems.recommendation: Oil leaks on the M276 are common but not usually urgent. If you notice oil on the undertray or a burning smell, have a specialist inspect the timing covers and camshaft sensors. The sensor seals are a straightforward fix; timing cover resealing is more labour-intensive but worthwhile if the car is otherwise healthy. Don't ignore persistent leaks - oil starvation is the quickest way to destroy an otherwise robust M276.

problems.rootCause: The M139l features an F1-derived electrically assisted turbocharger and a 48V mild-hybrid system. While these technologies promise better responsiveness and efficiency, they introduce additional complexity and potential failure points not present on the older V6.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt M139l engine with new turbo and 48V components

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2024-present GLC43 AMG 4MATIC is worth approximately £50,000-£70,000. Replacement cost is modest relative to vehicle value.
problems.recommendation: The M139l is too new for definitive reliability data. Early owner feedback is mixed - the engine delivers strong performance but the 48V system and electric turbocharger add complexity. If you're considering a GLC43, ensure the 48V battery health is checked and that the vehicle has a comprehensive warranty. For owners facing issues, specialist diagnostics are essential - not all independent workshops are equipped for M139l work.
